audit_scope.description: Batch 16 (final batch with 4 files) covers final EL components including exception handling, protocol validation, and boundary interactions. This completes Worker 0's processing of files 41-79 (batches 9-16).

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peers via DevP2P - General Protocol Interaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers send blocks, transactions, and state data over unauthenticated channels. All peer-provided data is untrusted and must be validated against consensus rules. Malicious peers can send invalid data attempting to cause crashes, consensus failures, or DoS. EL must handle all invalid inputs gracefully with proper exception handling.

trusted_external_entities.name: RPC Clients via JSON-RPC - General API Access
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External applications and users access EL via JSON-RPC over HTTP/WebSocket. Endpoints are typically unauthenticated or use basic auth. Clients can send malformed requests, invalid parameters, or attempt resource exhaustion via expensive queries. EL must validate all RPC inputs, enforce rate limits, and return proper error responses.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Originators - General Transaction Submission
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anyone can submit signed transactions via RPC or P2P propagation. Transaction signer is identified by signature recovery, but all transaction content is untrusted. EL must validate signature, nonce, balance, gas parameters, and execution validity. Invalid transactions must be rejected before mempool inclusion and block building.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: P2P protocol messages are untrusted. Block headers must be validated (all fields, parent hash, state root, receipts root, etc.). Transactions must be validated (signature, nonce, balance). State sync data must be verified against state root. Invalid messages trigger exceptions and peer disconnection. EL must not crash or enter inconsistent state on invalid peer data.

RPC requests are untrusted. Invalid JSON causes parsing errors. Invalid parameters cause validation errors. Expensive queries (large block ranges, trace requests) must be rate-limited. Authentication should be implemented for sensitive endpoints. Errors return JSON-RPC error objects with codes and messages. DoS via RPC must be prevented through rate limiting and resource caps.

All transaction fields are untrusted except signature-verified sender address. Must validate: signature recovers to valid address, nonce equals account's current nonce, sender balance >= value + (gas_limit * gas_price), gas_limit <= block_gas_limit, transaction type is supported, calldata is well-formed for transaction type. Execution must handle all EVM exceptions gracefully, consume gas correctly, and revert state on failure.
